subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat `toolErrorDelivery` policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: This changes both config surface and user-visible failure delivery: it would reduce hosted/team-chat noise, but it can also hide real failed mutations that the current policy intentionally surfaces.

options.title: Approve default-compatible final/off policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean path only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and close or narrow the final-only request to docs and channel-specific bugs.

options.title: Split concrete leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle remaining Feishu, exec-like detail, lifecycle-warning, or channel-specific leaks in narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible final/off policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged acknowledged-warning fix and explicitly scoped this issue as the remaining broader policy/config decision.
